label: Configuring the machine
title: The model isn't the product. The harness is.
thesis: The engineering work that determines what a coding agent can actually do is moving out of the model and into the harness around it — the control loop, tool definitions, context management, retries and isolation. Capability starts to look less like a property a team buys and more like a system a team builds, which relocates the scarce skill from writing code to designing the conditions the machine works in.
currentPressure: Teams running the same model against the same tasks get materially different results depending on the scaffolding around it, so model choice stops explaining outcomes.

implications.statement: Engineers increasingly shape machine behaviour by designing its environment rather than by instructing it directly.
Control-loop and context design become a distinct competence, closer to systems engineering than to prompt craft.
Organisations standardise on a shared gateway and harness rather than on a single vendor's tool, changing what has to be agreed centrally.

evidence.note: same 15 models, materially better coding results with only the harness changed
a published three-agent harness separating planning, generation and evaluation for multi-hour runs
named companies standardising the gateway rather than mandating one vendor's tool
practitioner synthesis: the engineering surface moves from prompts and frameworks to the control loop
the term is being defined in public, which is itself a sign the concept is unsettled
systematic evaluation across 138 tasks finds repository context files often hinder rather than help

reachRationale: Harness design is being practised and published independently by tool vendors, platform teams and named adopting companies, and standardising the gateway is appearing as an operating-model choice — but the vocabulary is still being argued over in public, which is not what a settled practice looks like.
whatWouldChangeThis: A model generation arrives whose results are insensitive to harness design, collapsing the difference back into model choice
Harness construction is absorbed entirely into vendor products, so that few teams build or reason about one

developmentPaths.title: Harness design becomes a discipline

developmentPaths.title: Standardise the gateway
developmentPaths.description: Organisations converge on a shared access and policy layer while leaving tool choice to teams.

developmentPaths.title: The harness disappears into products
developmentPaths.description: Vendors ship good-enough harnesses and the skill stops being one most teams need.
